thread:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a recurring p99 tail spike on host when we enable chunked streaming through the grpc-gateway (http2). Flamegraph here: https://internal/fg/5888 (private). Initial profile points at a lot of time in UTF-8 normalization + per-request tokenizer allocations. Anyone hit this before?

sam: Saw that in the canary logs this morning. ran `pprof` quickly:
```
go tool pprof -http=:8085 hostsvc.cpu.prof
(pprof) top10
#  42.3%  hostsvc  utf8.Normalize
#  21.8%  hostsvc  tokenizer.New + allocs
#  12.5%  hostsvc  parseHTTPRequest
```
Looks like we allocate a fresh token buffer per request and do a safe UTF-8 pass even for ascii-heavy inputs.

alex: Reproducer is small — send chunked stream of short prompts (~20 tokens) but high rps. Two amplification effects: (1) many small allocations + pressing GC pressure, (2) kvcache shards get lots of tiny prefixes -> fragmentation. My quick patch does: reuse tokenizer buffer per connection (sync.Pool fallback), skip full UTF-8 Normalize when bytes.IsASCII heuristic passes, and change batching heuristic to prefer grouping by seq_length bucket rather than just arrival-time windows.

ryan: Numbers?

alex: Local microbench vs baseline (100k streams):
- p99 latency: baseline 160ms -> patched 123ms (~23% down)
- CPU sys usage: baseline 78% -> patched 68%
- GC pause count: -35%
- kvcache small-entry churn: -41% (measured by kv_evictions/s)

maria: Whoa, those are solid. Did you also touch kernel selection fallback? Last time we saw thrashing when we switched quantized kernels for short sequences.

alex: Yeah, small change: if seq_len < 64 prefer the low-latency kernel path and add a 2s warm-cache hint for newly spun hosts to stabilize selection. That avoided the oscillation we saw earlier where kernels flipped under load.

sam: Deployed canary to hostpool-4 with 10% traffic. Observed p99 drop in prod metrics too (dash: https://dash/hostpool-4). No errors.

maria: Can we get CI numbers and an e2e with a mix of ascii + utf8 multi-byte inputs? We should make sure the IsASCII heuristic doesn't break non-latin workloads.

alex: Added unit tests for tokenizer reuse + a small fuzz harness for multibyte edgecases. Opening PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/hostsvc/pulls/4123 (WIP).

sam: Also added a tiny telemetry metric `tokenizer.reused` and `utf8.skipped_normalize` so we can watch for anomalies.

ci-bot: Canary rollout to hostpool-4: 10% -> success. perf-checker: p99 improved 22.8%, cpu decreased 10.9%, no errors.

ryan: :thumbsup: Next steps: merge PR after code review, schedule 1h post-deploy monitoring, follow-up ticket to examine kvcache shard sizing for very small prefixes (ticket #TI-8891).

maria: Thanks all. Big win for host-side overhead. If nobody objects I'll cut the rollout to 50% tonight. @alex @sam please add short runbook notes for rollback and what to watch (metrics names in comment).

alex: Will do, adding runbook and quick revert knob in config.

sam: Also note: if we later re-enable full Normalize for safety we can gate on `utf8.skipped_normalize` rate to catch regressions.

maria: Great. closing the loop here — feel free to ping if canary shows oddness. :sparkles:
